title: Common normal constants and induction of finite semilinear scheme actions
statement: Let $e$ be a field [def-weil-field], and let $I$ be a nonempty finite set. For each $i\in I$ let $F_i/e$ be a finite field extension [def-pc-field-extension] [def-pc-field-tower], let a finite group $J_i$ act on $F_i$ by $e$-automorphisms, and let $V_i$ be a finite-type $F_i$-scheme with a compatible semilinear $J_i$-action. Let $B_i$ be an $e$-scheme and $v_i:V_i\to B_i$ a $J_i$-invariant $e$-morphism [def-pc-scheme] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There are a finite normal extension $K/e$ with embeddings $F_i\hookrightarrow K$, a finite group $G$ with a surjection $G\to A=\operatorname{Aut}_e(K)$, and subgroups $\Gamma_i\leq G$ with surjections $\Gamma_i\to J_i$. The two actions on $F_i$ agree, so $\Gamma_i$ acts diagonally on $W_i=V_i\times_{F_i}K$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. The extension $K^G/e$ is purely inseparable. The induced scheme $Y_i=G\times^{\Gamma_i}W_i$ exists: it is the disjoint union of copies of $W_i$ indexed by left cosets of $\Gamma_i$, with scalar structure on the copy represented by $g$ twisted by the image of $g$ in $A$; the relation is $(g\gamma,w)\sim(g,\gamma w)$. Left multiplication gives a semilinear $G$-action, and $[g,w]\mapsto v_i(\operatorname{pr}_1w)$ defines an invariant $e$-morphism $Y_i\to B_i$. For every geometric point $b:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to B_i$ of $B_i$ [def-weil-geometric-point], if the underlying points of the geometric fibre $V_i\times_{B_i}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ of $v_i$ at $b$ form a nonempty single $J_i$-orbit, then the underlying points of the geometric fibre $Y_i\times_{B_i}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ of $Y_i\to B_i$ at $b$ form a nonempty single $G$-orbit. If $v_i$ sends every generic point to a generic point with finite residue extension, the same is true of $Y_i\to B_i$. Finite morphisms and generic points use [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-sc-generic-point], [def-weil-residue-field]; geometric fibres use [def-weil-geometric-fibre]. Normal for a finite field extension means that every irreducible polynomial over $e$ with a root in $K$ splits in $K$; no separability is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-common-normal-compatible-groups] to the given field actions. Choose its $K$, product group $G$, projection $\pi$, subgroups $\Gamma_i$ and maps $r_i$. This supplies all field and finite-group clauses, including $K^G/e$ purely inseparable and $\pi(\ker r_i)=\operatorname{Aut}_{F_i}(K)$ after identifying $F_i$ with its embedded image.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, (2.b); assembly from the independent lemmas cut from the retained ten-step proof.

proof.text: Fix $i$. On $W_i=V_i\times_{F_i}K$, define $\gamma$ by its action $r_i(\gamma)$ on $V_i$ and $\pi(\gamma)$ on $K$. Their restrictions agree on $F_i$, so [def-pc-fibre-product] gives the diagonal automorphism; uniqueness after the two projections proves the identity and multiplication laws. Its scalar map is $\operatorname{Spec}(\pi(\gamma)^{-1})$. The morphism $q_i=v_i\operatorname{pr}_1$ is invariant because $v_i$ is invariant.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, (2.b); assembly from the independent lemmas cut from the retained ten-step proof.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-semilinear-coset-scheme] to $(K,G,\pi,\Gamma_i,W_i,q_i,B_i)$. Its coproduct, relation, scalar formula, action and invariant map give the required $Y_i=G\times^{\Gamma_i}W_i$ and $Y_i\to B_i$, with precisely the stated twists and left action. Each input is over $e$ since every field automorphism fixes $e$.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, (2.b); assembly from the independent lemmas cut from the retained ten-step proof.

proof.text: For a geometric point $b$ with nonempty single $J_i$-orbit in $(V_i)_b$, apply [lem-sfb-normal-scalar-extension-geometric-orbits]. Its kernel condition is exactly the equality in step 1. It gives a nonempty single $\Gamma_i$-orbit in $(W_i)_b$, including inseparable or nonreduced fibres. The base-change and orbit assertion of [lem-sfb-semilinear-coset-scheme] then gives a nonempty single $G$-orbit in $(Y_i)_b.

source.place: X 2.3 Step 2, printed p.150, (2.b); assembly from the independent lemmas cut from the retained ten-step proof.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-finite-scalar-extension-generic-points], $W_i\to V_i$ sends component generic points to component generic points with finite residue extensions, and composing with $v_i$ preserves this property. The clopen copies given by [lem-sfb-semilinear-coset-scheme] have exactly the component generic points of their copies of $W_i$: the closure of a point stays in its clopen copy. On every copy the map to $B_i$ is $q_i$, regardless of its scalar twist. Hence $Y_i\to B_i$ has the required property.
